sections.title: Roller — every setting
sections.summary: A spinning wheel picker — the data type, the wheels and their values (text lists or number ranges), the selected-value label styling, and the picker container’s background, borders, corner radius and padding. This guide documents every setting of the Roller block, grouped by area. Each setting matches a real control in the screen editor.

sections.title: Roller section
sections.summary: The Roller section configures a spinning wheel picker that captures a visitor's choice — a date, age, size, or similar value — and saves it in a variable you can reuse for personalization or routing. Reach for it when an input has many ordered options that would be too many to show as buttons. It only appears on wheel-picker screens; add one from the canvas, then set the data type, wheels, and label styling here.

sections.title: Where it appears
sections.summary: Covered screen types: WheelPicker.

sections.title: Color of the picker outline
sections.summary: Color of the outline around the picker container (default light gray, #E0E0E0). Use a light neutral for a subtle card edge, or your accent color to make the picker stand out on the screen. It only shows when the border thickness above is greater than 0.

sections.title: Roundness of the corners
sections.summary: How rounded the four corners of the picker container are, in pixels (0-50, default 12). 0 gives sharp square corners; higher values look softer and more modern. Match it to the corner roundness of your buttons and other cards so the whole funnel feels consistent.

sections.title: Thickness of the picker outline
sections.summary: Width in pixels of the outline around the picker container (0-50, default 1). Set it to 0 for no border and rely on the background color alone, or use 1-2px for a clean, defined edge. The border color setting below only takes effect when this is greater than 0.

sections.title: Background behind the wheels
sections.summary: Fill color behind the spinning wheels (default white, #ffffff). Choose a color that contrasts enough with the screen background so the picker reads as its own distinct card and the wheel values stay legible. A subtle off-white or light tint often separates the picker from the page better than pure white.

sections.title: Space inside the picker
sections.summary: Sets the empty space, in pixels, inside the picker container on each side: top, right, bottom, left, between the border and the spinning wheels. The default is usually a small value; increase it to give the wheels breathing room, or keep it tight for a compact picker. A clean, uncluttered picker feels effortless to use, which helps visitors commit their answer and continue through the funnel.

sections.title: Text choices or numbers
sections.summary: Chooses what the picker collects: String for text choices, which allows up to 5 side-by-side wheels (such as month / day / year), or Integer for a single numeric range (such as age or quantity). Set this first — it limits Integer to one wheel, unlocks up to five wheels for String, and changes how each wheel's options are set up below.

sections.title: Pre-selected starting value
sections.summary: The value already showing when the screen loads. For List wheels, pick one of your options; for Range wheels, pick any number within the from/to span. Pre-selecting the most common answer reduces friction and prevents accidental empty or extreme submissions — leave it empty only if you truly want nothing chosen up front.

sections.title: Size of the selection label
sections.summary: Text size of the label that shows the user's current choice above the wheels (0-50, default 18). 16-22 keeps the chosen value clearly readable; very small or 0 effectively hides it. Increase it when you want the selection to stand out as a confirmation of what the user picked.

sections.title: Thickness of the label text
sections.summary: How heavy the selection label looks, from 300 (Light) to 900 (Black); default 400 (Regular). Use 600-700 (Semibold/Bold) to make the chosen value read as a clear confirmation, or keep it at 400 if it should sit quietly above the wheels. Match it to the weight of your other body text for a consistent look.

sections.title: Where the label sits
sections.summary: Horizontal position of the selection label within its container: left, center, or right (default center). Center usually lines up with the centered wheels and is the safe choice; switch to left or right only to align the label with other text or a specific layout. This is purely visual and does not change the value the user selected.

sections.title: Color of the selection label
sections.summary: Color of the label text that shows the user's current choice above the wheels (default black, #000000). Pick a color with strong contrast against the container background so the chosen value stays easy to read, ideally your theme's main text color for consistency. This affects only the label, not the wheel options themselves.

sections.title: Edit the wheel's choices
sections.summary: The text choices shown on a List-mode wheel. Add, edit, drag to reorder, or delete options (1-20 allowed). The order here is the order users scroll through, so place the most common choices near the top where the starting value lands. Each option is per-language, so translate them if your funnel runs in more than one language.

sections.title: Lowest number on the wheel
sections.summary: The smallest number a Range-mode wheel starts at. Together with the 'to' value it sets the span users can scroll — for example from 1 to 10 lets them pick any number from 1 through 10. Keep this lower than 'to', and set it to the smallest realistic answer for your question, such as a minimum age or quantity.

sections.title: Highest number on the wheel
sections.summary: The largest number a Range-mode wheel ends at. Together with the 'from' value it sets the span users can scroll — for example from 1 to 10 lets them pick any number from 1 through 10. Keep this higher than 'from', and set it to the largest realistic answer for your question so users aren't offered absurd values.

sections.title: Joiner between wheel values
sections.summary: The character or characters used to join selections from multiple wheels into one combined value — for example '/' turns two wheels into 'Large/Red', or a space joins them with a gap. This only matters when you have more than one wheel; leave it as-is for a single-wheel picker. Choose a separator that reads naturally in the answer you'll store and reuse later in the funnel.

sections.title: List of options or number range
sections.summary: Sets how this wheel's values are built: List means you type each option yourself (sizes, labels, months), while Range means you set a from/to span and the wheel fills in every number between, such as 1 to 10. Use List for arbitrary text choices and Range for evenly-spaced numbers. Note that switching between them clears the options you've already entered for this wheel.

sections.title: Add and set up wheels
sections.summary: The spinning wheels users scroll to make their choice. Each wheel is either a List of text options or a Range of numbers; use Add Wheel to add more (up to 5 with the String data type, only 1 with Integer), then expand a wheel to set its type, options, and starting value. Each wheel's selection is saved as a variable you can reuse later for personalized copy or to route users down different paths.

translations.en: Roller — every setting

A spinning wheel picker — the data type, the wheels and their values (text lists or number ranges), the selected-value label styling, and the picker container’s background, borders, corner radius and padding. This guide documents every setting of the Roller block, grouped by area. Each setting matches a real control in the screen editor.

en.name: The screen editor with the Roller section highlighted.

translations.en: Open the Roller section in the screen editor to configure its settings.
Wheels & values

nodes.label: Wheels & values · Text choices or numbers

translations.en: Text choices or numbers

Chooses what the picker collects: String for text choices, which allows up to 5 side-by-side wheels (such as month / day / year), or Integer for a single numeric range (such as age or quantity). Set this first — it limits Integer to one wheel, unlocks up to five wheels for String, and changes how each wheel's options are set up below.

en.name: Where to find “Text choices or numbers” in the editor.

nodes.label: Wheels & values · Joiner between wheel values

translations.en: Joiner between wheel values

The character or characters used to join selections from multiple wheels into one combined value — for example '/' turns two wheels into 'Large/Red', or a space joins them with a gap. This only matters when you have more than one wheel; leave it as-is for a single-wheel picker. Choose a separator that reads naturally in the answer you'll store and reuse later in the funnel.

en.name: Where to find “Joiner between wheel values” in the editor.

nodes.label: Wheels & values · Add and set up wheels

translations.en: Add and set up wheels

The spinning wheels users scroll to make their choice. Each wheel is either a List of text options or a Range of numbers; use Add Wheel to add more (up to 5 with the String data type, only 1 with Integer), then expand a wheel to set its type, options, and starting value. Each wheel's selection is saved as a variable you can reuse later for personalized copy or to route users down different paths.

en.name: Where to find “Add and set up wheels” in the editor.

nodes.label: Wheels & values · List of options or number range

translations.en: List of options or number range

Sets how this wheel's values are built: List means you type each option yourself (sizes, labels, months), while Range means you set a from/to span and the wheel fills in every number between, such as 1 to 10. Use List for arbitrary text choices and Range for evenly-spaced numbers. Note that switching between them clears the options you've already entered for this wheel.

nodes.label: List of options or number range

en.name: Where to find “List of options or number range” in the editor.

nodes.label: Wheels & values · Edit the wheel's choices

translations.en: Edit the wheel's choices

The text choices shown on a List-mode wheel. Add, edit, drag to reorder, or delete options (1-20 allowed). The order here is the order users scroll through, so place the most common choices near the top where the starting value lands. Each option is per-language, so translate them if your funnel runs in more than one language.

en.name: Where to find “Edit the wheel's choices” in the editor.

nodes.label: Wheels & values · Lowest number on the wheel

translations.en: Lowest number on the wheel

The smallest number a Range-mode wheel starts at. Together with the 'to' value it sets the span users can scroll — for example from 1 to 10 lets them pick any number from 1 through 10. Keep this lower than 'to', and set it to the smallest realistic answer for your question, such as a minimum age or quantity.

en.name: Where to find “Lowest number on the wheel” in the editor.

nodes.label: Wheels & values · Highest number on the wheel

translations.en: Highest number on the wheel

The largest number a Range-mode wheel ends at. Together with the 'from' value it sets the span users can scroll — for example from 1 to 10 lets them pick any number from 1 through 10. Keep this higher than 'from', and set it to the largest realistic answer for your question so users aren't offered absurd values.

en.name: Where to find “Highest number on the wheel” in the editor.

translations.en: Pre-selected starting value

The value already showing when the screen loads. For List wheels, pick one of your options; for Range wheels, pick any number within the from/to span. Pre-selecting the most common answer reduces friction and prevents accidental empty or extreme submissions — leave it empty only if you truly want nothing chosen up front.

en.name: Where to find “Pre-selected starting value” in the editor.

translations.en: Selection label styles

nodes.label: Selection label styles · Size of the selection label

translations.en: Size of the selection label

Text size of the label that shows the user's current choice above the wheels (0-50, default 18). 16-22 keeps the chosen value clearly readable; very small or 0 effectively hides it. Increase it when you want the selection to stand out as a confirmation of what the user picked.

en.name: Where to find “Size of the selection label” in the editor.

nodes.label: Selection label styles · Thickness of the label text

translations.en: Thickness of the label text

How heavy the selection label looks, from 300 (Light) to 900 (Black); default 400 (Regular). Use 600-700 (Semibold/Bold) to make the chosen value read as a clear confirmation, or keep it at 400 if it should sit quietly above the wheels. Match it to the weight of your other body text for a consistent look.

en.name: Where to find “Thickness of the label text” in the editor.

nodes.label: Selection label styles · Color of the selection label

translations.en: Color of the selection label

Color of the label text that shows the user's current choice above the wheels (default black, #000000). Pick a color with strong contrast against the container background so the chosen value stays easy to read, ideally your theme's main text color for consistency. This affects only the label, not the wheel options themselves.

en.name: Where to find “Color of the selection label” in the editor.

nodes.label: Selection label styles · Where the label sits

translations.en: Where the label sits

Horizontal position of the selection label within its container: left, center, or right (default center). Center usually lines up with the centered wheels and is the safe choice; switch to left or right only to align the label with other text or a specific layout. This is purely visual and does not change the value the user selected.

en.name: Where to find “Where the label sits” in the editor.

translations.en: Picker container styles

nodes.label: Picker container styles · Background behind the wheels

translations.en: Background behind the wheels

Fill color behind the spinning wheels (default white, #ffffff). Choose a color that contrasts enough with the screen background so the picker reads as its own distinct card and the wheel values stay legible. A subtle off-white or light tint often separates the picker from the page better than pure white.

en.name: Where to find “Background behind the wheels” in the editor.

nodes.label: Picker container styles · Thickness of the picker outline

translations.en: Thickness of the picker outline

Width in pixels of the outline around the picker container (0-50, default 1). Set it to 0 for no border and rely on the background color alone, or use 1-2px for a clean, defined edge. The border color setting below only takes effect when this is greater than 0.

en.name: Where to find “Thickness of the picker outline” in the editor.

nodes.label: Picker container styles · Color of the picker outline

translations.en: Color of the picker outline

Color of the outline around the picker container (default light gray, #E0E0E0). Use a light neutral for a subtle card edge, or your accent color to make the picker stand out on the screen. It only shows when the border thickness above is greater than 0.

en.name: Where to find “Color of the picker outline” in the editor.

nodes.label: Picker container styles · Roundness of the corners

translations.en: Roundness of the corners

How rounded the four corners of the picker container are, in pixels (0-50, default 12). 0 gives sharp square corners; higher values look softer and more modern. Match it to the corner roundness of your buttons and other cards so the whole funnel feels consistent.

en.name: Where to find “Roundness of the corners” in the editor.

nodes.label: Picker container styles · Space inside the picker

translations.en: Space inside the picker

Sets the empty space, in pixels, inside the picker container on each side: top, right, bottom, left, between the border and the spinning wheels. The default is usually a small value; increase it to give the wheels breathing room, or keep it tight for a compact picker. A clean, uncluttered picker feels effortless to use, which helps visitors commit their answer and continue through the funnel.

en.name: Where to find “Space inside the picker” in the editor.
